one_line: Auditable human-agent security finding review room.
what_it_does: Presents structured security candidates, evidence and provisional agent recommendations for human validation, rejection, and rationale logging.
leverage_rationale: Shared structured findings, evidence-bound recommendations, and agent-inaccessible final decisions make the agent materially more reliable than UI-driving for an auditable review workflow.
leverage_evidence: Devpost screenshot visibly shows Findings, Evidence, Agent recommendation, and Human decision sections.
Screenshot states human decision is not exposed to agent tools and shows Validate/Reject controls.
execution_rationale: The packet and screenshot show a coherent review-room surface with multiple findings and decision controls, but no video or end-to-end completion evidence is supplied.
execution_evidence: Devpost screenshot shows SecureFlow review-room UI with three findings and review controls.
Gallery packaging lists five workflow screenshots, but the supplied frame-sheet evidence is repetitive and does not clearly prove completion.
impact_rationale: Security teams have a concrete need to distinguish real vulnerabilities from alerts and document accountable remediation decisions.
impact_evidence: Pitch targets evidence review, scope validation, risk assessment, and remediation documentation.
Screenshot shows a concrete authorization finding and reviewer rationale requirement.
creativity_rationale: The evidence-first human-agent security review framing is a fresh synthesis with meaningful governance depth.
creativity_evidence: Project explicitly separates provisional agent recommendations from human decisions.
Audit-oriented review-room workflow is more specific than a generic security chatbot.
usability_note: The visible review layout is organized, though small text and unverified flow leave usability uncertain.
red_flags: No submitted video; frame evidence does not clearly demonstrate an end-to-end action.
standouts: Evidence-bound recommendations with agent-inaccessible final human decision.
advance_reason: Strong, specific human-agent security review concept with credible visible product evidence.

what_it_does: Lets agents inspect, create, organize, modify, and propose changes to structured workspace plans while humans approve, reject, and undo them.
leverage_rationale: The claimed shared application state, approvals, and undo make WebMCP central rather than merely a chat or UI automation layer.
leverage_evidence: Pitch says UI and agent use the same underlying application state.
Description names project, task, planning, approval, and undo tools.
execution_rationale: The workspace concept is coherent, but there are no frame sheets, gallery images, or video to substantiate the central workflow beyond packaging text.
execution_evidence: Packet reports live demo but no submitted video or gallery images.
Description claims visual workspace, agent panel, activity log, approval, and undo workflow.
impact_rationale: Teams and individuals can benefit from agents operating on plans while retaining review and reversibility.
impact_evidence: Pitch gives a concrete product-launch planning use case.
Human approval and undo address a real trust and coordination need.
creativity_rationale: A workspace designed simultaneously for human and agent users is a fresh interaction model, though depth is not visually evidenced.
creativity_evidence: Project frames the agent as a second workspace user, not only a conversational assistant.
Approval and undo are integrated into the proposed collaboration model.
usability_note: Likely approachable from the described workflow, but no visual evidence was submitted.
red_flags: No submitted visual or video evidence.
advance_reason: Promising concept, but the packet lacks sufficient execution evidence for advancement.

one_line: Agent-native shopping with bounded visual product context.
what_it_does: Combines structured commerce tools with targeted product-image references so multimodal agents can compare appearance and fit before shopping actions.
leverage_rationale: Bounded image tools improve agent access to relevant visual context, but a capable general multimodal agent could achieve much of the same outcome with friction.
leverage_evidence: Description specifies structured catalog/cart/checkout tools and five bounded vision tools.
Project targets product-specific visual comparison rather than noisy full-page screenshots.
execution_rationale: The demo is reported dead and no visual workflow evidence was submitted, so execution is capped despite a detailed description.
execution_evidence: Packet reports demo_alive=dead.
No video, frame sheets, or gallery images submitted.
Devpost screenshot shows descriptive story content, not a running product.
impact_rationale: Visual fit and finish decisions are a real shopping problem for users and agents, especially for home and design purchases.
impact_evidence: Description gives concrete room-style and finish-selection use cases.
Structured compatibility and checkout extend beyond a toy visual search.
creativity_rationale: The deliberate two-tier commerce-plus-vision interaction is a fresh, well-articulated angle on shopping agents.
creativity_evidence: Five named vision tools provide a specific interaction model.
Temporary browser photo URLs and explicit user-photo selection show attention to bounded visual context.
usability_note: The described flow is understandable, but the dead demo prevents usability assessment.
red_flags: Demo reported dead; no submitted product evidence.
standouts: Focused visual-decision layer rather than pretending structured commerce data is enough.
advance_reason: Interesting concept but execution and eligibility cannot be established from the packet.

one_line: Agent-assisted arranging studio with musical guardrails and human taste decisions.
what_it_does: Writes instrumental parts into notation, rejects unreachable notes and invalid bars, derives transpositions, supports listening choices, edits, locks, and exports.
leverage_rationale: The page and agent share live notation, range, transposition, bar arithmetic, locks, and human-choice state that a general UI-driving agent could not reliably manipulate comparably.
leverage_evidence: Transcript demonstrates a rejected trumpet D6 with a reason, followed by agent octave correction.
Transcript shows human-selected endings, locked bars, skipped writes, shared timeline, and exports.
Frame sheets visibly show notation editor, multi-part score, playback, and side-panel workflow.
execution_rationale: The 152-second video transcript and frame sheets demonstrate a coherent end-to-end workflow from brief to score, validation, listening, editing, and export.
execution_evidence: Transcript explicitly covers setup, writing parts, refusal/correction, listening, locking, hand edits, timeline, and MusicXML/MIDI export.
Frame sheets show rendered multi-part notation and playback/editor states.
impact_rationale: School band directors have a specific, labor-intensive arranging problem, and the product directly produces playable parts for children.
impact_evidence: Transcript identifies real ensemble constraints and manual rewriting burden.
Transcript states exported trumpet parts can be read by 30 children tomorrow.
creativity_rationale: The concept deeply integrates agent writing, formal music constraints, and deliberately human-only listening judgment into a memorable interaction model.
creativity_evidence: Page refusal is an active musical guardrail that returns an actionable correction reason.
ask_human hands aesthetic choice back because the model cannot hear; locks and shared timeline pursue the concept deeply.
usability_note: The demonstrated workflow is legible and purpose-built for directors, with clear correction and review affordances.
standouts: Constraint-aware agent writing with human listening as a first-class boundary.
advance_reason: Exceptional evidence-backed WebMCP fit, execution, impact, and originality.

what_it_does: Uses WebMCP to answer provenance questions, explain edits and creators, and trace content histories based on C2PA credentials.
leverage_rationale: Structured provenance queries can make technical credential history conversational and precise, though the same information could be extracted by other agent integrations with friction.
leverage_evidence: Description names questions about origin, edits, AI involvement, and tracing originals.
Frame sheets reportedly show provenance-oriented product states and media examples.
execution_rationale: The packet presents a coherent product and three frame sheets, but lacks transcript and clear end-to-end tool invocation evidence.
execution_evidence: Description gives a concrete C2PA conversational workflow.
Frame sheets are submitted, but no transcript is available and visual details are limited.
impact_rationale: Creators, journalists, platforms, and everyday viewers have a real need to understand digital content provenance as synthetic media grows.
impact_evidence: Description identifies concrete provenance questions and the usability gap in technical metadata.
C2PA provenance is a credible trust and media-literacy use case.
creativity_rationale: Turning provenance metadata into a conversational, traceable interface is a notably original and timely interaction model.
creativity_evidence: Project explicitly asks questions of content history rather than manually opening metadata tools.
The concept covers capture through editing and back to originals.
usability_note: Conversational questions could lower the provenance barrier; actual interaction quality is only partly evidenced.
red_flags: No video transcript or direct tool-call evidence.
standouts: Accessible conversational layer over C2PA provenance histories.
advance_reason: Clear audience need and original provenance interaction with adequate, if incomplete, product evidence.

what_it_does: Lets an agent inspect an incident and fill a shared rollback form while the operator edits scope and submits; server checks prevent stale or widened operations.
leverage_rationale: WebMCP makes the current page's shared, constrained recovery-plan state available to the agent while preserving a genuine human submit boundary; generic UI driving cannot replicate this reliably.
leverage_evidence: Transcript records actual page-registered tool calls inspect_current_incident and show_change_comparison.
Agent fills but cannot submit the declarative Recovery Plan; human removes healthy payment and submits.
Transcript demonstrates stale-plan refusal and server-side allowlist checks.
execution_rationale: The 164-second video demonstrates a complete incident-to-recovery workflow, including real deployment verification, human edit, stale handling, and successful recovery.
execution_evidence: Transcript states real Cloudflare deployment, fixed request changing 500 to 200, and RECOVERED only after verification.
Frame sheets show incident-room UI and agent/page workflow states.
impact_rationale: On-call teams face high-stakes rollback decisions where faster investigation and explicit human review directly reduce operational risk.
impact_evidence: Transcript identifies the concrete failure mode of chat approvals changing production before review.
Demonstrated workflow narrows scope, blocks stale plans, and verifies recovery.
creativity_rationale: The project turns the browser page into a shared, constrained operational control surface and makes approval semantics substantive rather than cosmetic.
creativity_evidence: No-toolautosubmit boundary and human-edited plan are central interaction design.
Stale-plan refresh and server allowlist are unusually deep treatment for a challenge demo.
usability_note: The workflow is explicit and safety-oriented, with the operator retaining scope and submission control.
standouts: Real rollback verification and safety boundaries.
Shared page state makes human review operationally meaningful.
advance_reason: Best-in-class demonstrated WebMCP leverage, safety-conscious execution, and operational impact.

one_line: Nested local-first planning board for people and agents.
what_it_does: Uses nested folds, bounded reads, atomic plan creation, trace paths, shared selection, and exports to keep complex plans manageable for humans and agents.
leverage_rationale: Bounded depth/pagination, current-level context, selection-aware edits, and atomic batches address agent context and precision problems beyond ordinary UI automation.
leverage_evidence: Description names 18 tools and bounded reads with depth, pagination, and description caps.
Shared human drag edits and agent edits operate on the same local-first board.
Trace and selection-aware changes reduce screenshot/object-reference ambiguity.
execution_rationale: Three frame sheets and a detailed description show a coherent board concept and workflows, though no video proves the complete flow.
execution_evidence: Frame sheets visibly show nested-board UI states.
Description specifies atomic creation, folds, trace, edits, and four export formats.
impact_rationale: People planning moves, projects, or systems can benefit from reducing large-map overload while retaining structure and exportability.
impact_evidence: Description identifies cognitive/context overload for both people and agents.
Examples span house moves and user stories, with JSON/PNG/Mermaid/Markdown exports.
creativity_rationale: Folds as a bounded-context planning primitive are a distinctive interaction model that is pursued across human and agent workflows.
creativity_evidence: Nested levels and cross-fold trace replace the conventional infinite canvas.
Agent receives compact, scoped context rather than an unbounded board export.
usability_note: Folds and scoped views plausibly improve readability, with direct drag interaction and multiple exports.
red_flags: No video transcript; agent invocation is described but not directly shown in supplied evidence.
standouts: Bounded context is designed into the board model, not added as an agent prompt.
advance_reason: Strong agent-native planning model with visible product evidence and credible utility.

one_line: Observability and evaluation dashboard for WebMCP apps.

leverage_rationale: WebMCP is both the monitored subject and the dashboard's shared investigation surface; structured tool-call traces and agent-driven evidence navigation materially exceed UI automation.
leverage_evidence: Description names SDK trace capture, CLI CI evals, release joins, and a dashboard with 38 tools.
Agent can switch views, set filters, inspect sessions, draft eval cases, and save after approval.
execution_rationale: The packet describes a substantial coherent observability workflow and supplies three frame sheets, but no video or transcript demonstrates the claimed end-to-end sequence.
execution_evidence: Frame sheets visibly show dashboard/analytics UI states.
Description specifies incidents, releases, sessions, regression explorer, cases, and eval pull workflow.
impact_rationale: Teams building WebMCP apps need regression detection and production traceability to make agent interactions dependable.
impact_evidence: Pitch directly targets production traces, CI evals, and regressions across app/model/tool versions.
Description gives concrete investigation and case-generation workflow.
creativity_rationale: Combining WebMCP observability, production traces, CI evaluation, and conversational investigation is a strong and relevant synthesis.
creativity_evidence: Dashboard is itself a WebMCP app with agent navigation and approval.

one_line: Privacy-first synthetic ledger with agent-assisted review and draft entries.
what_it_does: Shows fictional cash flow and transactions, lets an agent read summaries/list records/create a draft, and lets a person review the in-memory draft.
leverage_rationale: Explicit schemas and reversible session-only drafts make agent interaction safer and more structured, but the small ledger outcome remains feasible through ordinary UI automation.
leverage_evidence: Description names three narrowly scoped tools for summary, transactions, and fictional draft creation.
Human review occurs before the draft is added to in-memory session state.
execution_rationale: The concept is bounded and coherent, but no visual or video evidence demonstrates the ledger workflow.
execution_evidence: Packet reports no video or gallery images.
Description specifies summary, filters, categories/budgets, draft review, and in-memory store.
impact_rationale: It offers a safe educational/prototyping experience for exploring agent finance workflows without exposing real financial data, though the synthetic scope limits direct utility.
impact_evidence: Project explicitly targets privacy and avoids accounts, storage, and external integrations.
Synthetic cash-flow review and draft entries are a concrete bounded use case.
creativity_rationale: Privacy-first synthetic finance is a sensible angle, but the interaction is a modest take on a familiar ledger workflow.
creativity_evidence: Clear synthetic/session-only boundary and explicit reversible tools.
No evidence of a substantially novel interaction model.
usability_note: The intentionally small scope should be understandable, but it cannot be assessed visually from the packet.
red_flags: No submitted visual or video evidence.
Synthetic-only data limits demonstrated real-world workflow depth.
standouts: Strong privacy boundary and narrow reversible tool contracts.
advance_reason: Coherent safe demo, but insufficient evidence and limited novelty/impact for advancement.
